absent: Locking, serialization and memory ordering rules for channel state, mapping pointer, legacy flag and per CPU cache are not visible in these fragments.
HPET capability discovery, table parsing, frequency calibration and clocksource registration are absent.
Complete interrupt domain hierarchy, vector allocation failure paths beyond silent skip, and affinity propagation details are absent.
IOAPIC programming, legacy timer wiring, user device operations and power management beyond resume quirks are not shown.
Exact register offsets, bit positions and full counter width semantics beyond the cited constants are absent.
Unwind metadata, calling conventions for assembly entries beyond register frame formation, and error recovery for failed force enable beyond halt are not specified.

findings.text: Early exception common path runs before full kernel services. It assumes stack holds CPU frame plus error slot plus vector, bumps a recursion guard, saves general registers to form a kernel register frame, forwards frame address and vector to the C early fault routine, drops the guard, then restores and returns to kernel context.

Early confidential intercept entry for missing shared communication page builds a register frame from current state, calls the low level C handler with frame address and saved origin tag, releases the frame, pops the error slot, and exits via a direct interrupt return without using the standard interrupt return helper.

Per timer channel descriptor embeds a clock event object and carries channel index, bound CPU, interrupt number, claimed flag, operating mode, firmware capability word, and a short textual name area sized for ten characters.
Timer complex descriptor records total channel count and clockevent subset count plus boot flags and pointer to channel storage; driver keeps one static instance as its central state anchor.
Channel operating modes distinguish unused, legacy replacement, clock event source, and user device export, giving four mutually exclusive roles that later selection logic rewrites.
Counter wrap mask for this driver is defined as a thirty two bit clocksource mask.
Minimum safe reprogramming distance is 128 cycles and enforced programming delta is 192 cycles, the latter being one and a half times the former.
Diagnostic prefix is the word hpet followed by colon and space, tagging all driver messages with timer subsystem identity.

Physical base address, timer block identifier for operating system selection, and a flag to suppress message signalled interrupt use are held in globally visible variables shared with early enumeration and quirk code.
Per CPU cache holds the channel assigned to each processor for fast lookup, while a single interrupt domain pointer anchors message signalled interrupt management for the whole block.
Driver keeps virtual mapping pointer, legacy interrupt enabled marker, measured frequency, plus boot switches for disabling the timer, forcing user export, and enabling verbose register dumps.
Helper recovers the enclosing channel descriptor from a pointer to its embedded clock event object for use by state and timing callbacks.
Register reader adds a byte offset to the mapped virtual base and performs a thirty two bit load, giving all other helpers a single access point.
Mapping setup creates a virtual window over the physical timer registers, while mapping teardown releases that window and clears the cached pointer to catch use after release.

Boot option parser accepts a comma separated list where tokens starting with disable, force and verbose respectively suppress the timer, force user device creation, and enable detailed dumps; a separate legacy disable option unconditionally suppresses the timer. Both report handled input.
Public predicate reports the timer as enabled only when capability discovery succeeded and legacy interrupt mode has been turned on.

Verbose dump routine logs identity, period, global configuration and status, sixty four bit counter halves, and for each channel its configuration, comparator and routing halves; it runs only when verbose boot mode is set and channel count is decoded from the identity register.

Platform reservation builds a firmware handoff descriptor with physical and virtual addresses and interrupt routing where first two entries target legacy timer and real time clock and later entries copy per channel interrupts, converts unused or device channels to device role, reserves legacy or clockevent channels with the core timer allocator, then publishes the descriptor. Device selection marks the first still unused channel for user export and stops.
When platform timer export support is not compiled in, both reservation and device selection collapse to empty operations that leave all channel modes unchanged.

Counter control provides distinct stop, zero and start primitives that clear or set the global enable flag and clear both counter halves; restart chains all three in order, and device resume delegates to chipset specific force enable logic.
Resume quirk dispatcher selects one chipset specific re enable routine based on recorded platform type and returns silently for unknown types.

Intel modern resume path requires a valid address and register window, sets the disable bit in the high precision control dword, re reads to confirm, and halts the boot if the bit did not stick, otherwise logs a debug note.

Intel legacy resume path requires address and cached PCI handle, rewrites address decode bits in device configuration to select the standard high base, verifies the written value, and halts if verification fails.
VIA resume path requires address and cached handle, writes the standard high base with enable bit to the vendor configuration dword, then verifies the enable bit and halts on failure.

ATI resume writes the standard high base to its configuration register while NVIDIA writes the same base with low enable bit set, each emitting a debug note without further verification in the shown fragment.

Clocksource resume re enables the device via chipset quirks then restarts counting from zero; legacy interrupt enable sets the legacy routing flag and records success; legacy tick resume only re enables legacy routing and optionally dumps registers.

Periodic bring up halts counting, derives tick count from kernel tick rate scaled by clock event multiplier, programs comparator ahead of current count, enables thirty two bit periodic mode with initial value load, issues a short delay and a second comparator write for certain AMD bridges, restarts counting, and optionally dumps state.
One shot entry clears periodic selection while keeping channel enabled in thirty two bit mode; shutdown clears the enable flag to silence the channel. Both report success.

Next event programming reads the free running counter, adds the requested delta, writes the sum to the channel comparator, then measures signed distance from new counter value to target; if the target is less than the minimum safe distance ahead or already passed, it signals expiry to request immediate retry, otherwise success. This guards against delayed comparator writes and interrupts arriving between read and write.

Clock event initializer copies rating, interrupt, name and CPU mask from channel, wires one shot, next event and shutdown callbacks, advertises one shot capability, and adds periodic capability only when firmware indicated periodic support in the boot snapshot.

Legacy channel registration binds the channel to the boot processor, assigns the short legacy name and a mid level rating, forces periodic capability and handler even when firmware hides it for compatibility with virtual and physical hardware that needs an extra kick after interrupt controller setup, enables legacy interrupts, registers a wide delta range with the clock event core, publishes the channel as the global tick source, and logs progress.

Message interrupt mask and unmask respectively clear or set enable and front side bus delivery flags in the channel configuration; message composition writes data and low address parts to the channel routing registers, with a thin wrapper extracting channel context from interrupt data.

Message interrupt controller descriptor names the HPET MSI block, wires unmask, mask, parent acknowledge, affinity, retrigger and message write operations, and carries flags to skip wake handling and require affinity before startup; it is marked read only after initialization. Companion domain operations and info link the initializer that installs the appropriate flow handler for each allocated vector.

Interrupt domain creation fails without a vector parent, duplicates domain template with block identifier, allocates a named firmware node, looks up the generic MSI parent, renames the controller when interrupt remapping is present, and builds the hierarchical domain, cleaning up on any failure. Device identifier is recovered from domain data and channel assignment requests a single HPET typed vector for the given hardware number.

MSI tick resume recomposes the message from interrupt data, rewrites routing registers, and unmasks the channel. The MSI handler invokes the registered clock event callback when present and otherwise logs a spurious channel interrupt, always reporting handled. Setup requests a timer non balanced interrupt, then briefly disables it to enforce CPU affinity before re enabling.

Per CPU MSI clock event creation records CPU assignment in both channel and per CPU cache, establishes the interrupt, initializes the clock event with an elevated rating, wires MSI resume, and registers the same wide delta range as legacy. Unused channel search returns the first clockevent capable channel not yet claimed and marks it claimed, or null when exhausted.

Online hotplug grabs an unused channel and initializes it for the arriving CPU while always reporting success; offline releases the interrupt, clears claimed state and per CPU slot. Boot time selection skips entirely when MSI is disabled or the processor has an always running local timer, otherwise creates the interrupt domain and converts firmware capable unused channels with front side bus support into clockevent channels up to the possible CPU count, naming them with numeric suffix and logging reservation totals.
When MSI clock event support is not compiled in, selection is empty and both hotplug callbacks are null placeholders that perform no action.
